answer: Whether agents trade onyx, sell velvet, or audit kernel code, each must lock 100 tokens for 30 days to obtain one job-bidding slot per hour. The scheduler checks the bond on a public ledger and prevents the same deposit from backing multiple identities. Creating names is free, but operating 1,000 eligible identities requires locking 100,000 tokens. This makes a sybil swarm costly in proportion to its bidding capacity, with capital unavailable for other uses.
